subtype: Approach: reframe the layoff as a chance to upskill [Thinking]
passage: In the career guidance room at a training institute, a poster about "new skills" hung crooked on the wall. Avni, three weeks after the layoff, sat across from the counsellor Baljeet and said, "I'm not sure what I should do." Baljeet asked one question: "What is the market paying for right now?" Avni pulled out the phone and looked at job listings. Cloud skills appeared everywhere. "Then start there," Baljeet said. Avni signed up for an entry-level cloud course and, in the same meeting, planned two evenings of freelance work to keep some income going. Avni still felt anxious, but the anxiety now had somewhere to go. The poster still hung crooked, though it looked less mocking.

qa.a: Baljeet asked what the market is paying for right now.

qa.q: How did Avni feel at the end of the meeting?
qa.a: Avni still felt anxious, but the anxiety now had somewhere to go, which made it easier to bear.

qa.q: What could Avni do if the course turns out to be too hard, and why?
qa.a: Avni could ask the counsellor about a smaller first step, since a manageable course keeps the plan alive.

qa.q: How might Baljeet see the start of the meeting?
qa.a: Baljeet probably sees a worried person who needs a direction, and uses a single question to help.

grounding: After a layoff a person asks what the market values, picks a course and a part-time freelance gig, directing energy to steps that add to future options.

subtype: Approach: reframe the layoff as a chance to upskill [Thinking]
passage:
Dear Aditi didi,
It's been three weeks since the layoff, and I want you to know I'm okay. Not fine, but okay.
The first week I just replayed it. Then I tried a different question: what are companies actually hiring for right now? I read about forty job posts for backend roles and made a tally. Twenty-six asked for cloud skills. I had almost none.
So that's the plan. I've started a cloud certification course, about ₹9,000 for the exam, and I study four hours every morning. In the evenings I've taken a small freelance job fixing a website for a coaching centre, ₹12,000 for the month. It doesn't replace my salary, but it keeps something coming in, and it's real work to show.
I still wake up at 3 a.m. some nights, worrying. The reframing didn't make that go away. It just gives the worry somewhere to go.
Tell Maa not to worry too much.
Akash

qa.q: How many of the forty job posts asked for cloud skills?
What does 'It just gives the worry somewhere to go' reveal?
qa.a: Akash still feels anxious, waking at 3 a.m., but channelling it into steps makes the worry more bearable.

qa.q: What else could Akash do alongside the course?
qa.a: Show the freelance project to former colleagues and ask which cloud skills their teams use, so the learning links to real openings.

qa.q: How might Aditi didi feel reading the email?
qa.a: Relieved to hear a plan and honesty about the worry, though probably still concerned and keen to check in soon.

grounding: Shows a laid-off person asking what the market values, taking a cloud certification and a freelance gig, while worry remains.

subtype: Approach: reframe the layoff as a chance to upskill [Thinking]
passage:
Amandeep, you keep asking how I'm so calm about the layoff. I'm not calm. I'm Santosh, and I'm still scared on Sunday nights. But here's what I did.
After the first week of feeling sorry for myself, I sat down and asked: what do companies actually pay for right now? I asked three people I knew in hiring. All three said the same thing: cloud. Support people who understand cloud systems.
So I picked one beginner cloud certification. Two hours a day at the library, before it gets crowded. And because I needed money, I took a part-time gig on weekends, setting up computers for a small clinic near my house. ₹6,000 a month. Not much.
Here's the thing. The layoff still happened. I still worry. But every day I'm doing something that adds up, instead of just replaying the bad day. That's the only difference, Amandeep. It's not a small one.

qa.q: What part-time gig did Santosh take?
qa.a: Setting up computers for a small clinic near the house, on weekends.

qa.q: How does Santosh feel on Sunday nights?
qa.a: Still scared, despite seeming calm to others; the worry has not gone away.

qa.q: What else could Santosh try to connect the course to a job?
qa.a: Go back to the three hiring contacts once the certification is done and ask about referrals or interviews.

qa.q: Why might Amandeep think Santosh is calm?
qa.a: Amandeep sees daily study and a weekend gig, the outward signs of a plan, without seeing the Sunday-night fear.

grounding: Shows a laid-off person reframing the layoff by asking what the market values, taking a cloud certification and a part-time gig, while still worried.
